header.running_head: Hadhrat Umar (RA) Consults with Men of knowledge

blocks.text: Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) Consult with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and the Good Comments that Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) made about him

Hadhrat Ataa bin Yasaar reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to call for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and consult with him along with those Sahabah (RA) who participated in the Battle of Badr (the senior Sahabah (RA)). During the periods of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) used to issue Fataawaa (rulings) and did so until he passed away.

Hadhrat Ya'qoob bin Zaid narrates that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) used to consult with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) about every matter of importance and would say to him, "Dive into the matter, dear diver (because he was capable of reaching the essence of the problem at hand)."

Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) said, "I have not seen any person as quick-witted, as intelligent, as knowledgeable and as tolerant as Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA). I have seen Umar (RA) summon him to solve intricate problems and say, 'An intricate problem has presented itself to you.' Umar (RA) would then do only what Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) proposed even though he was surrounded by Muhaajireen and Ansaar who had participated in the Battle of Badr." [^1]

Hadhrat Ibn Shihaab reports that whenever an intricate problem presented itself before Hadhrat Umar (RA), he would summon some young men to consult and choose to act according to the sharpness of their intellect. [^2]

Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) would engage in so much consultation that he would even consult women (when the need arose). In fact, there were several occasions when he liked the opinions that they expressed and acted on it. [^3]
A Remarkable Lecture of Hadhrat Umar (RA) Concerning Consultation

Hadhrat Muhammad, Talha and Ziyaad all report that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once left Madinah and dismounted at an oasis called Siraar (3 miles from Madinah) where he instructed that the army comes to a halt. The soldiers did not know whether he intended to camp there or proceed further. Whenever the Muslims intended to know something from Hadhrat Umar (RA), they always sent either Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) or Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA).
